title: Raja ne apna maans kyun kaata?
hooks: Raja ne apni jaang ka maans kaat diya — kabootar ke liye
Ek raja ne apna maans tol diya, sirf ek kabootar bachane
Indra ke devtaon ne raja ki daya pariksha li, phir ye hua
hook_why: Opens with the most shocking visual — a king cutting his own flesh — and names the named entity (king) in the first 4 words, matching the raaz hook rule and Jain katha hook rule for immediate curiosity.
metaphor: Weighing scale (tula) balancing the pigeon against the king's own flesh — visual metaphor for compassion outweighing self-preservation.
mechanism: Indra sends two demi-gods as pigeon and hawk to test king's compassion
Pigeon seeks refuge on king's lap
King offers own flesh to save pigeon
King refuses: butcher would kill another animal
King cuts flesh from thigh, hawk demands equal weight
Weighing scale brought: pigeon vs flesh pieces
King keeps cutting flesh, scale still tips to pigeon
King sits on scale himself in meditation
Scale balances, demi-gods reveal true forms

cast.King Megharath: crowned ancient Indian king, golden crown with central jewel, calm compassionate face, beige silk dhoti with gold border, seated on marble throne in Jain palace hall with carved pillars and shikhara spires visible through arches
cast.Pigeon: white pigeon with gentle eyes, small and delicate, feathers slightly ruffled
cast.Hawk: large brown hawk with sharp talons and piercing eyes, fierce presence
cast.Courtier: elderly minister in white cotton dhoti and angavastram, folded hands, concerned expression
cast.Demi-gods: two radiant celestial beings in white silk dhotis, golden ornaments, glowing aura, folded hands in reverence

scenes.vo: Raja maans kat-kat ke rakhta gaya, kam padta raha, ant mein khud tula pe baith gaya, dhyan laga liya

scenes.vo: Kabootar-baaz bane devta, raja ko aashirwad diya, yehi atma bani Shantinath — 16ve Tirthankar. Tum kya karte? Jai Jinendra

caption:
Raja Megharath ne apna maans kaat diya sirf ek kabootar bachane. Ye daya hi unhe Shantinath banayi. 🙏

Srot: Jain kathayein

Tum hote to kya karte?

claims.claim: King Megharath cut his own flesh to save a pigeon from a hawk
claims.basis: Jain kathaon per jainknowledge.com and jainworld.com sources

claims.claim: The pigeon and hawk were demi-gods testing the king's compassion
claims.basis: Both sources state Indra sent two demi-gods in these forms

claims.claim: King refused butcher's meat to avoid causing another animal's death
claims.basis: Direct quote from sources: 'The butcher may have to kill another animal'

claims.claim: King sat on the weighing scale himself when flesh was insufficient
claims.basis: Sources: 'Finally the king was getting ready to put his whole body on the scale'

claims.claim: King Megharath's soul became the 16th Tirthankar Shantinath
claims.basis: Both sources explicitly state this at the end of the story
